open_points.subject: authorization of snapshot import results
open_points.text: “Project-scoped access requires … project grant/assignment” conflicts with R0-21: “The read needs only the authenticated bearer credential … it does not recheck the producer's project grant or the Registry lifecycle.”
open_points.question: Is an import result a project-scoped record; if so, is R0-21 an explicit exception to invariant 2, or must its read recheck project access?
options: Import results are project-scoped, but ownership by the importing principal is an explicit authorization exception
Import results are project-scoped and require the current producer grant and Registry lifecycle check
Import results are principal-scoped rather than project-scoped
open_points.default_guess: Treat import results as principal-scoped records that retain project provenance and follow the explicit R0-21 ownership check.

witness.initial: A producer imported a snapshot for project P, received import_id I, and its grant for P was later revoked.
events: The producer authenticates with a valid bearer credential and requests I.
outcomes: Invariant 2 denies the read because the project grant is gone.
R0-21 returns I because the same principal made the import and no grant is rechecked.

open_points.subject: archived-project allocation and mapping records
open_points.text: “An archived project's budget, snapshot, expense, document, progress, payment and photo records are readable and immutable” does not name expense allocations, budget-section mappings, or budget activation state, although they are separate persistent facts elsewhere.
open_points.question: Are allocations, section-mapping decisions, and activation state included in the immutable archived-project record set?
options: All are frozen and readable after archival
Allocations are part of expense records, while mappings and activation state are part of budget records
Some remain mutable after archival
open_points.default_guess: Freeze and retain all project-bound allocation, mapping, and activation facts.

witness.initial: Project P is archived with an expense allocated to section S and a saved section mapping.
events: An assigned operator attempts to reallocate the expense or alter the mapping.
outcomes: The mutation is rejected because these facts are included in the archived project's expense and budget records.
The mutation is allowed because invariant 5 and R0-24 do not expressly name allocations or mapping decisions.

open_points.subject: producer grants on archived projects
open_points.text: Invariant 5 says existing grants “keep giving access,” but R0-24 forbids snapshot import for an archived project and R0-21 says import-result reads do not use the producer grant.
open_points.question: What access, if any, does an existing producer grant continue to confer after project archival?
options: No usable operation; the grant is retained only so it can be revoked
It permits some project read operation that the text has not named
It permits import-result reads, contrary to R0-21's statement that the grant is not checked
open_points.default_guess: State that a producer grant is retained and revocable but confers no usable operation while the project is archived.

witness.initial: Producer S has a grant for project P, and P is archived.
events: S attempts a new snapshot import.
S reads an old import result.
An administrator revokes S's grant and S reads the result again.
outcomes: The grant keeps giving some access, as invariant 5 states, but the operation is unnamed.
Import is rejected, and both result reads succeed independently of the grant, so the grant gives no access.

open_points.subject: OCR-only expense creation
open_points.text: R0-05 says “an Expense is created only through OCR intake,” while R0-17 says the portal trusts a staff submission and “does not verify independently that the content came from the OCR service.”
open_points.question: Is OCR provenance an enforceable precondition for expense creation, or is any authenticated staff submission in the recognition-result shape sufficient?
options: Any authorized staff submission is sufficient; OCR-only is an operating convention
The portal must verify an OCR-issued assertion or reference before creating an expense
A separate intake principal must attest provenance once Q12 is resolved
open_points.default_guess: Narrow the OCR-only promise to an operating convention until a verifiable intake hand-off exists.

witness.initial: An operator has mutation capability for project P but no OCR output.
events: The operator constructs a syntactically valid confirmed recognition result with an invented provenance_ref and submits it.
outcomes: R0-17 accepts it because the authenticated submission is trusted.
R0-05 rejects it because it did not come through OCR intake.

open_points.subject: first-administrator audit
open_points.text: R0-07 says creation of the first administrator is “never … audited,” while invariant 12 and the Audit section require every significant action, including staff-account management, to carry actor provenance to audit.
open_points.question: Is first-administrator bootstrap an explicit exception to the audit invariant, or must it create an audit record?
options: Bootstrap is explicitly exempt from product audit
Bootstrap writes a product audit record with a host-operator actor representation
Bootstrap writes a separate host audit outside the portal
open_points.default_guess: Make bootstrap an explicit exception to product audit and require a separately defined host audit if operational traceability is wanted.

witness.initial: The deployment has no staff accounts.
events: A host operator successfully runs the bootstrap command.
outcomes: No audit record exists, as R0-07 requires.
A staff-account creation audit record exists, as the Audit section and invariant 12 require.

open_points.subject: bootstrap command result contract
open_points.text: R0-07 promises “a closed set of exit codes that deployment scripts may branch on” but does not enumerate the codes or their meanings.
open_points.question: What are the complete bootstrap exit codes, and which code represents success, an existing staff account, invalid input, configuration failure, and persistence failure?
options: Enumerate distinct stable codes for each branch
Use success plus one generic failure code
Use success, already-initialized, invalid-input, and internal-failure categories
open_points.default_guess: Use stable categories for success, already initialized, invalid input, and operational failure.

events: A deployment script invokes the bootstrap command.
outcomes: The command returns a dedicated already-initialized code that the script treats as benign.
The command returns a generic failure code that the script treats as a deployment failure.

open_points.subject: bootstrap secret input channel
open_points.text: R0-07 says email and password are read “neither from process arguments nor from the environment nor from a file” but does not name the channel from which they are read or its non-interactive behavior.
open_points.question: How does the host operator supply the bootstrap email and password, and what happens when that channel is unavailable or reaches EOF?
options: Interactive controlling-terminal prompts with hidden password entry
A structured standard-input protocol
A local privileged IPC or secret-agent channel
open_points.default_guess: Use controlling-terminal prompts and fail with a defined code when no terminal is available.

witness.initial: An empty deployment is being initialized by non-interactive automation.
events: Automation invokes the bootstrap command without a controlling terminal.
outcomes: The command reads a defined standard-input protocol and succeeds.
The command requires an interactive terminal and fails.

open_points.subject: staff password validity
open_points.text: R0-07 and R0-19 accept an initial password, but no decision states which password values are valid beyond storing them with argon2id.
open_points.question: What password policy is applied to bootstrap, staff creation, password change, reset completion, and recovery-related flows, and are all of those actions governed by the same policy?
options: A single explicit length and allowed-character policy applies everywhere
Only a minimum length is enforced
Any non-empty value is accepted
open_points.default_guess: Apply one explicit length-based policy uniformly and permit all Unicode characters.

witness.initial: An administrator creates a staff account with the initial password “a”.
events: The creation request is authorized and otherwise valid.
outcomes: The account is created because no password restriction is stated.
The request is rejected under an implementer-selected strength policy.

open_points.subject: staff email normalization
open_points.text: Staff login requires a “unique normalized email,” while R0-07 and R0-19 accept an email input without defining normalization or equality.
open_points.question: What exact normalization and comparison rule determines whether two staff email addresses are the same login identifier?
options: Trim and compare the entire address case-insensitively
Lowercase only the domain and preserve local-part case
Use a specified Unicode and IDNA normalization procedure
open_points.default_guess: Trim surrounding whitespace, normalize the domain with IDNA, and compare the full resulting address case-insensitively.

events: An administrator attempts to create user@EXAMPLE.COM.
outcomes: Creation is rejected as a duplicate after case-insensitive normalization.
Creation succeeds because the local part is treated as case-sensitive.
witness.observer: The administrator and both prospective account holders

open_points.subject: liveness and readiness semantics
open_points.text: R0-11 says the service answers unauthenticated liveness and readiness checks but does not state what makes each check pass or fail, or what their observable success and failure responses are.
open_points.question: Which conditions determine liveness and readiness, and what stable status/body does each condition produce without disclosing forbidden details?
options: Liveness checks only the process; readiness checks validated configuration, database access, and binary-root access
Both checks report only whether the HTTP process can respond
Readiness also depends on Registry availability
open_points.default_guess: Make liveness process-only and readiness depend on validated local configuration, writable database access, and readable binary storage, but not Registry availability.

witness.initial: The HTTP process is running, but its SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: An orchestrator calls liveness and readiness.
outcomes: Liveness passes and readiness fails.
Both checks pass because the process can answer HTTP.

open_points.subject: concealed binary-read failure
open_points.text: R0-12 says unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize, or unlisted reads are “answered the same way” without naming that answer; it also does not classify missing or unreadable referenced bytes.
open_points.question: What exact concealed response is returned for protected-binary denial, and are a missing file, unreadable file, or content-detection failure part of the same concealed class?
options: A uniform not-found JSON error with no binary metadata
A uniform authorization-denied response
A uniform empty response with a fixed status
open_points.default_guess: Return the same not-found JSON response for all denied, absent, unreadable, oversize, and unrecognized objects.

witness.initial: One authorized record points to a missing file; another requested object exists but is hidden.
events: The same authorized caller requests each download.
outcomes: Both receive the same concealed not-found response.
The hidden object receives the concealed response, while the missing file produces an internal or storage-specific failure.

open_points.subject: deferred challenge responses
open_points.text: R0-15 and R0-23 use “the concealed authentication rejection” and “answers as usual” without defining the observable status, body, headers, timing obligations, or whether a reset-request response is identical for existing and absent accounts.
open_points.question: What exact public response contract applies to each inert challenge operation and to the inert password-reset request?
options: All inert confirmations share one fixed concealed rejection; every reset request shares one fixed accepted response
Each operation has its own fixed response while still concealing account existence
All operations return one generic response
open_points.default_guess: Define one fixed concealed rejection for confirmations and one fixed accepted response for every reset request, independent of account existence.

witness.initial: One reset request names an existing account and another names an absent email.
events: An unauthenticated caller submits both requests.
outcomes: Both receive the same fixed successful-looking response.
Implementers choose different ordinary responses or headers even though both requests do nothing.

open_points.subject: initial staff-password handoff
open_points.text: R0-19 says “The administrator hands the initial password to the holder outside the portal” but names no permitted handoff boundary, security requirement, confirmation, or failure outcome.
open_points.question: What external handoff is relied upon, what security properties must it have, and what happens when the holder never receives or loses the password?
options: The handoff mechanism is explicitly outside product scope with no product guarantee
Only an approved secure organizational channel may be used
The administrator replaces the initial password through another audited action
open_points.default_guess: Declare the handoff organizationally controlled and outside the product, and allow an administrator to set a fresh initial password through a defined audited action before first login.

witness.initial: An administrator creates and activates a pending staff account.
events: The administrator sends the initial password through an external channel, but the holder does not receive it.
outcomes: The administrator can replace the initial password through a defined product action.
The account remains unusable because only the deferred email reset or an exceptional recovery override could restore access.

open_points.subject: Registry validation versus concurrent archival
open_points.text: R0-24 promises “no new viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant is created for an archived project” because creation validates that the project is active, but it does not define what happens if Registry archives the project between validation and the local commit.
open_points.question: At what event is the no-new-access-after-archival rule evaluated, and what consistency mechanism or accepted race semantics apply across Registry and the portal?
options: The active result is a point-in-time precondition, so a concurrent archival race may still commit
Creation must revalidate immediately before commit
Registry must provide a reservation, version, or atomic conditional operation
open_points.default_guess: Define Registry validation as a point-in-time precondition and explicitly acknowledge the unavoidable race unless Registry supplies a versioned conditional contract.

witness.initial: Project P is active and an administrator begins creating a viewer grant.
events: The portal validates P as active.
Registry archives P.
The portal attempts to commit the grant.
outcomes: The portal commits because validation succeeded, creating access after archival.
The portal rechecks or conditionally commits and rejects the creation.

open_points.subject: recorded snapshot-import attempts
open_points.text: R0-25 records “every import attempt it classifies” and includes “a rejection,” but does not define which authenticated failures count as classified attempts rather than transport or parsing failures.
open_points.question: For which failure stages must the portal create an immutable import result and import_id—for example invalid JSON, missing fields, unsupported contract version, invalid project_id, failed authorization, Registry failure, or persistence failure?
options: Every authenticated request reaching the import route is recorded, including malformed payloads
Only payloads that can be parsed into the minimum snapshot envelope are recorded
Only domain validation outcomes after authorization and Registry validation are recorded
open_points.default_guess: Record attempts once authentication succeeds and a parseable minimum envelope identifies the intended import; handle earlier parsing failures as ordinary request errors.

witness.initial: A valid producer credential is used with malformed JSON on the import route.
events: The service authenticates the bearer credential and fails to parse the body.
outcomes: A rejection import result with a fresh import_id is persisted and returned.
No import result is persisted because the request could not be classified.

open_points.subject: snapshot content identity and fingerprint
open_points.text: R0-25 and the import rules distinguish “identical content” from “different content” using a content fingerprint, but do not define canonical content, field normalization, treatment of unknown fields, or decimal and ordering equivalence.
open_points.question: Which fields and canonicalization rules determine whether a republication is identical?
options: Fingerprint canonical JSON after schema validation, including every contract field
Fingerprint semantic normalized values and ignore JSON member order and representation differences
Fingerprint the received bytes exactly
open_points.default_guess: Fingerprint a version-specific canonical representation of all accepted contract fields, with normalized decimals and object-key ordering while preserving section order.

witness.initial: An accepted snapshot used amount 10.0 and one JSON member order.
events: The producer republishes the same business values as 10.00 with JSON members reordered.
outcomes: The request is an idempotent replay because semantic canonical content is equal.
The request is an integrity conflict because the received representation or fingerprint differs.

open_points.subject: import response status contract
open_points.text: R0-25 says the portal “answers the import request with that result” but does not state whether accepted, replayed, conflicted, and rejected results use success or error transport statuses, or the minimum fields common to every returned result.
open_points.question: What observable HTTP status and minimum response fields correspond to each import-result outcome?
options: Every classified attempt returns a successful transport response containing an outcome discriminator
Accepted and replay outcomes use success statuses; integrity conflict and rejection use error statuses while still returning import_id
Every fresh result uses a creation status regardless of its outcome
open_points.default_guess: Use success statuses for accepted and idempotent replay, domain-appropriate error statuses for conflict and rejection, and always include import_id plus the outcome discriminator for classified attempts.

witness.initial: A producer republishes an existing snapshot identity with different content.
events: The portal records a fresh integrity-conflict import result.
outcomes: The HTTP request returns a conflict status with the import result body.
The HTTP request returns a success status because recording the attempt succeeded, with conflict represented only in the result.
